Definition: from G3820; to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete:--decay, make (wax) old.
BiblicalUsage: Palaioō is to make old, to wear out, to declare obsolete. The heavens shall wax old as a garment, the first covenant is made old and ready to vanish away, and Jesus says to sell what you have and give alms, providing bags which wax not old.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word marks what time wears out and what it cannot touch. Covenants, heavens, and money-bags wear out, but the treasure in heaven never does.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
